compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

The weekly `Live External Integration` workflow (`.github/workflows/external-integration.yml`, cron `0 6 * * 1`) has been red on every scheduled run since 2026-09-28 (runs 36386577850, 37272823662, 38212894464, 39209787247, 40279678220, 41398914029). In every one, the only failing job is `langfuse tracing round-trip (ephemeral self-hosted)`, and it fails at `docker compose -f docker-compose.langfuse.yml up -d` with `minio Error unauthorized: access to the requested resource is not authorized`. That leaves the Langfuse tracing lane with no live coverage and hides any new failure in the other 9 jobs behind a run that is always red.

Found by the 2026-11-02 read-only ops sweep (session a85e3cd3).

### Root cause, per reported failure

1. **MinIO pull.** `docker-compose.langfuse.yml:118` pins `quay.io/minio/minio:RELEASE.2025-09-07T16-13-09Z`, set by `stoppable-sorry-budgie` after Docker Hub dropped `minio/minio`. quay.io now refuses anonymous access to that repository: `https://quay.io/api/v1/repository/minio/minio` returns 401 `invalid_token`, and the registry manifest request returns 401 even with an anonymous pull token. Control probes with the same method against public quay repositories (`prometheus/prometheus`) return 200, so the probe is sound. A local `docker pull` of the pinned tag fails with `401 UNAUTHORIZED`. No credential is configured for quay.io in the workflow, and adding one would make a public test stack depend on a private account.
2. **`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` unset: not reproduced.** In all 6 failing runs the secret-check step passed: its env shows `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ***` (GitHub's mask for a non-empty value), the next step ran, and `external LLM (live anthropic)` succeeded. The only `::error::` text about the key in the logs is the echoed script source of that check, not an emitted annotation. The secret is set; no change is needed for it. The workflow's own policy (`.github/workflows/external-integration.yml:33-41`) is that a missing credential FAILS loudly rather than skips, and the Langfuse job's check (`:354-362`) already follows it, so a future missing secret stays a visible, explicitly reasoned failure.

## Approach

Repoint the Langfuse MinIO service to `cgr.dev/chainguard/minio`, pinned by its multi-arch index digest: `cgr.dev/chainguard/minio@sha256:3c60a2a8c4d33409a9bc7a623a7fcbfb4605adc3d89422d2f53b3f673a6e5597` (platforms `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`).

Why this fits:
- It is the image upstream Langfuse's own `docker-compose.yml` (langfuse/langfuse `main`) uses for this service, with the identical `entrypoint: sh` and `mkdir -p /data/langfuse && minio server ...` command, so the repo stays aligned with the stack it emulates.
- It is anonymously pullable: the cgr.dev manifest request returns 200.
- Chainguard's free tier publishes only `latest` and `latest-dev` tags. The image-pin gate (`scripts/check_uv_pin.py:460`, `_check_image_reference`) rejects `:latest`, including `:latest@sha256:...`, and accepts a bare digest (`tag None, digest set`). A bare digest is therefore the only form that is both pullable and gate-compliant, and it is immutable, so the weekly run cannot change images without a commit.
- The service's `entrypoint`, `command`, environment, ports, volume, and `mc ready local` healthcheck stay unchanged; only the `image:` line and its explanatory comment change.

Riskiest assumption, already tested before planning: that the Chainguard image runs the repo's shell-entrypoint command and healthcheck. A local run of the digest-pinned image with that exact entrypoint and command created `/data/langfuse` and passed `mc ready local` immediately (`minio version RELEASE.2026-10-23T20-06-51Z`). A full local `docker compose up -d` of `docker-compose.langfuse.yml` with only the MinIO image overridden brought all 6 services up, and both CI readiness probes passed: `/api/public/health` after 5 tries and `/api/public/projects` with the headless-init keys after 1 try.

Portability: the change is an image reference in a Compose file that runs wherever Docker runs, on both amd64 and arm64; it adds no CI-only trigger.

## Scope

- `docker-compose.langfuse.yml`: the `minio` service's `image:` line and its comment.
- `tests/unit/test_langfuse_compose_images.py` (new): regression test for the MinIO image reference.

## Testing

Written first and run against the unfixed tree to confirm it fails:
- Happy path: `test_langfuse_minio_image_is_chainguard_digest_pin` loads `docker-compose.langfuse.yml` with `yaml.safe_load` and asserts `services.minio.image` matches `^cgr\.dev/chainguard/minio@sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$`. On `origin/main` it fails, because the value is `quay.io/minio/minio:RELEASE.2025-09-07T16-13-09Z`.
- Edge: `test_langfuse_minio_image_carries_no_tag` asserts the repository part before `@` has no `:` tag, so `cgr.dev/chainguard/minio:latest@sha256:...` (which the pin gate rejects) is caught by name here too.
- The existing gate suite `tests/unit/test_uv_pin_guard.py` and `python scripts/check_uv_pin.py` confirm the new reference passes the repo-wide image-pin gate.

No autouse fixtures and no new test helpers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `services.minio.image` in `docker-compose.langfuse.yml` is `cgr.dev/chainguard/minio@sha256:3c60a2a8c4d33409a9bc7a623a7fcbfb4605adc3d89422d2f53b3f673a6e5597`; verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_langfuse_compose_images.py` passing, after it was observed failing on the unfixed tree.
- [ ] The image-pin gate accepts the tree: `python scripts/check_uv_pin.py` exits 0 and `pytest tests/unit/test_uv_pin_guard.py` passes.
- [ ] `make lint` (with the worktree `.venv/bin` first on `PATH`) exits 0.
- [ ] [non-codebase] The change lands through Gerrit: the change number, `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1` vote outcomes, and the merged SHA on `origin/main` are recorded as a ticket comment.
- [ ] [non-codebase] The first scheduled `Live External Integration` run on `main` after both this fix and the deceptive-banal-baboon change land shows `langfuse tracing round-trip (ephemeral self-hosted)` past `docker compose -f docker-compose.langfuse.yml up -d` with no MinIO pull error, and the workflow concludes `success`; the run id, per-job conclusions, and timestamp are recorded as a ticket comment, read-only, without dispatching a run.
